sbc_memo: StockBasedComp is verified NIL across the entire FY2018-H1 FY2026 series. Delegat is ~66% family-controlled (Delegat/Douglas families) with no option scheme or LTI plan. The SBC owner-FCF adjustment (Step 1b) is therefore a genuine no-op: reported_fcf == owner_fcf before the lease-principal adjustment described below, and shares outstanding are flat at 101.13m throughout the projection with zero dilution and zero buybacks.
lease_liability_treatment: TotalDebt in the Metrics.csv is BANK BORROWINGS ONLY (~$323.4m at H1 FY2026). IFRS-16 lease liabilities (vineyard land leases, operationally essential) are held separately and were queried from the duckdb kpis table: FY2019 $86.4m -> FY2022 peak $124.3m -> H1 FY2026 $101.2m. Per repo precedent (2CC.NZ, TAH.NZ), lease liabilities are (a) included in net debt alongside bank debt, and (b) the lease PRINCIPAL repayment (not the full lease liability) is deducted from owner FCF each projected year, offsetting the ROU depreciation that was added back in the D&A step. This is not double-counting: the D&A add-back on right-of-use assets is non-cash only if the cash-equivalent (lease principal repayment) is separately deducted. FY2023's $45.1m lease repayment spike (Dashwood vineyard land purchase, buying out a lease) is a one-off excluded from the normalized lease_principal_pct path.

historical_growth.fcf_cagr_note: Reported FCF swung from -$9.1m (FY2024) to +$59.3m (FY2025) on the vineyard capex cycle taper - CAGR is not meaningful over any window spanning FY2021-24 due to sign changes. SBC is nil so reported FCF == owner FCF before the lease adjustment.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (5yr 7.7%, 3yr 5.5%) diverges >30% above Revenue CAGR (5yr 2.8%, 3yr 2.4%) and is directly contradicted by EPS CAGR (5yr -5.6%, 3yr -8.0%). This divergence is a structural feature of Delegat's economics, not a data error: high historical ROE (9-13%) with a ~40% payout ratio means retained earnings compound book value even while revenue stagnates and EPS declines through the FY2023-25 downturn. Using equity CAGR as the growth driver would silently assume a 7-8%/yr revenue growth path the business has not delivered since FY2020 and management's own guidance (3.3m->3.6m cases by FY2028, ~4%/yr case growth) does not support. Revenue CAGR is used as the primary driver per the instruction to reflect through-cycle reality; FY2018 is excluded from the primary CAGR window as it predates IFRS-16 adoption and sits on a different accounting basis (IFRS-15 restated: $255.8m vs as-filed $272.1m).

base.entry_price_correction_note: Terminal value rebuilt at the hurdle rate 2026-09-01: min(Gordon@hurdle, cap x FCF_N). The superseded value held the WACC-built terminal value and varied only the discounting.

sensitivity.methodology_note: Standard Gordon-growth-only sensitivity (uncapped) to show genuine WACC/terminal-growth directional sensitivity. The headline base-case valuation instead uses min(EV/EBITDA-anchored TV, 14x FCF cap) because at DGL's WACC levels pure Gordon growth on FCF (owner FCF is only ~48% of EBITDA after heavy capex/D&A/lease drag) implies an EV/EBITDA multiple of only ~3.5-4.5x - below the low end of DGL's own 8-year trading history (7.3x-16.4x, including the depressed FY2025 trough) - which failed the Step 8c sanity check (see sanity_check block) and was diagnosed and corrected. This sensitivity table is Gordon-only for transparency and will show lower values than the headline scenarios at matching WACC/g.

probability_weighted.note: Bear-case IV is negative (-$0.49/share), reflecting genuine mechanical downside: a shrinking-revenue, margin-compressed scenario against $408m of net debt (bank debt + IFRS-16 lease liabilities) at a 14.8% WACC. This is analogous to the accepted negative weighted-IV precedent for AGL.NZ elsewhere in this project - it signals leverage risk in a structural-decline tail scenario, not a modeling error, and is retained un-floored for transparency.

wacc_rationale.note: The Analysis.json dcf_notes_for_analyst suggested a +6% to +10.5% stacked premium (landing near 17.5-22% total, consistent with ALF.NZ/CDI.NZ/AGL.NZ comparables). An initial pass at that level (18.0% base WACC) combined with DGL's genuine net debt of $408.2m (bank debt $323.4m + IFRS-16 lease liabilities $101.2m, less cash $16.4m) produced a NEGATIVE base-case intrinsic value - a Step 8c sanity-check failure, since DGL is a going concern with 5.0x interest cover (FY2025) and positive, growing owner FCF, not a distressed shell like ALF.NZ (dead core business post-NZFL sale) or AGL.NZ. The WACC was recalibrated down to a base of 12.8% (a more moderate ~3.3% total stacked premium over a 9.5% NZ small-cap floor) to avoid implying insolvency for a profitable, well-covered business, while still carrying real premiums for illiquidity, family control, brand concentration, vintage variability and tariff risk. This remains materially above the ~8.6% WACC the market's current price of $4.20 implicitly assumes on the same base-case FCF path (solved by bisection), so the model is still conservative relative to the market's own risk pricing.

trip_check.initial_result: Base-case WACC of 18.0% (upper end of the Analysis.json-suggested +6% to +10.5% stacked premium band) combined with Gordon-growth terminal value produced a NEGATIVE base-case intrinsic value (-$0.45/share) and a Gordon-implied terminal EV/EBITDA multiple of only ~3.5x - roughly half the historical trough of 7.3x and a fraction of the 12.7x historical average (ex-FY2024). This failed the sanity check: it implies a going-concern, 5x-interest-cover business is worth less than zero, which is not credible.
trip_check.diagnosis: Two compounding effects: (1) DGL's owner-FCF/EBITDA conversion is structurally low (~45-50%) due to heavy vineyard capex, D&A and IFRS-16 lease-principal drag, so a Gordon-growth multiple applied to FCF (e.g. 9x) implies a much lower EBITDA multiple (~4-5x) than the market has ever paid for this business, even at its FY2025 trough (7.3x); (2) the top-of-range stacked WACC premium (+6.5-10.5%) suggested for distressed/near-dead comparables (ALF.NZ, AGL.NZ) is too punitive for DGL, which remains solidly profitable with 5.0x interest cover and management guiding NPAT UP to $60-62m for FY2026.
trip_check.fix_applied: (a) Recalibrated base WACC down from 18.0% to 12.8% (moderate ~3.3% total stacked premium over a 9.5% floor, still above the ~8.6% the market currently implies); (b) changed the terminal-value methodology from 'lower of Gordon vs FCF-multiple cap' to 'lower of EV/EBITDA-anchored TV (12.69x, the historical average ex-FY2024) vs a 14x FCF-multiple cap', using Gordon growth for disclosure/sensitivity only. This keeps the FCF-multiple cap as the binding, conservative constraint in all three scenarios (base/bull/bear) while anchoring the ceiling to a demonstrated market-clearing multiple rather than an algebraically punitive Gordon output.
trip_check.residual_conservatism_note: Even after the fix, the base-case implied EV/EBITDA (6.2x) and P/E (6.0x) sit BELOW the historical trough (7.3x / 8.0x at FY2025), i.e. the model remains conservative rather than aggressive relative to the company's own worst-priced year. This reflects deliberately below-FY2025-peak margins in the base case (34% EBITDA margin vs FY2020/21's 38.6%) and a WACC still above the market's own implied discount rate.

implied_multiples.note: Multiples of the INITIAL failing model (base IV -$0.45 at 18.0% WACC, Gordon TV). Retained for audit.

valuation_philosophy.summary: DGL.NZ is a profitable, real-brand, cash-generative but heavily levered and structurally-challenged small-cap. The DCF is built bottom-up from EBITDA margin recovery (32.5% FY2025 actual -> 34% mid-cycle, still below the 38.6% FY2020/21 peak) through a component FCF build (D&A, capex tapering to FY2026 guidance levels, IFRS-16 lease principal, and revenue-growth-scaled working capital reflecting wine's long ageing/inventory cycle). Terminal value uses the lower of an EV/EBITDA multiple anchored to DGL's own 8-year trading history (ex the FY2024 tariff/vintage outlier) and a 14-15x FCF-multiple ceiling, because a pure Gordon-growth approach on FCF (as opposed to EBITDA) systematically understates value for capital-intensive businesses with heavy D&A/capex/lease drag - it was tested, failed the Step 8c sanity check by implying negative equity value for a going concern, and was replaced. WACC (12.8% base) carries real but moderated stacked premiums for illiquidity, family control, brand concentration, vintage risk and tariff exposure - still above the ~8.6% the market's own price implies, so the model remains a conservative read on the business rather than a bullish one. Net debt of $408.2m (bank debt + IFRS-16 lease liabilities) is a genuine structural headwind: even the base case shows -30% downside to the current $4.20 price, and only the bull scenario (tariff relief sustained, North America recovery, margin recovery to 38%) clears the current price.

key_bull_drivers: Feb-2026 Supreme Court IEEPA tariff ruling + June-2026 guidance upgrade to $60-62m Operating NPAT
H1 FY2026 EBITDA +6%, gross margin 49% vs 48%, net debt down $38.6m half-on-half
Capex tapering from $59.9m (FY25) to $26.2m (FY26 guided) frees cash for debt paydown/dividends
Oyster Bay brand leadership (#1-2 premium Sauvignon Blanc in key markets, #1 NZ wine brand in China, China +41% FY25)
UK/Europe (+12%) and APAC (+16%) case volumes re-accelerating in H1 FY2026
key_bear_drivers: 24-Jul-2026 Section 301 'forced labour' tariff regime replaces the struck-down IEEPA tariff at a HIGHER effective ~17% total rate - tariff risk is relabelled, not resolved, and FY2026 full-year results (due late Aug-2026) are the first real read
Structural, secular decline in global wine consumption (health/moderation trends, weak Gen Z engagement) acknowledged by management itself
Single-brand/varietal concentration (Oyster Bay Sauvignon Blanc dominates earnings)
~66% Delegat family control + thin free float = governance/liquidity discount with no activist/M&A pathway
$307-408m net debt (incl. leases) and $200m+ inventory/biological WIP amplify a demand-shock or poor-vintage downside

The $60-62m Operating NPAT guidance (June-2026 upgrade) is management's own forecast, not an audited actual, and should be treated as a signal rather than a base-year fact.
